goal: Keep csv-report a reliable internal tool that turns the weekly CSV export into a summary report, choosing the CSV processing approach that fits its deployment and maintenance reality.
question: Select the CSV processing approach for csv-report that best fits its current role as a single-script internal tool producing a weekly summary report from the CSV export: keep the standard-library implementation or add a data-handling dependency.
known_constraints: The tool runs as a single script on the analyst's laptop (README.md).
Nobody has measured how large the weekly files get; sizes vary a lot between weeks (README.md).
The script currently processes the CSV with only the Python standard library csv module (process.py:1-12).
The repository has no dependency manifest and no tests (repository listing, checked 2026-10-01).

environment.deployment: single script run on the analyst's laptop
environment.current_behavior: reads export.csv from the working directory and prints the row count

evidence: process.py imports only csv from the standard library; summarize() counts rows with a generator expression, so it streams input with roughly constant memory (process.py:1-12).
The module docstring records the current intent: 'Turn the weekly CSV export into a summary report (stdlib only today).' (process.py:1)

README describes the tool as internal, run as a single script on the analyst's laptop, and states that nobody has measured how large the weekly files get while sizes vary a lot between weeks (README.md:1-5).

The repository contains exactly README.md and process.py plus a .claude skills directory; there is no pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, setup.py, lock file, test suite, or CI configuration (repository listing, checked 2026-10-01).

alternatives.name: Keep Standard Library csv Only
alternatives.description: Continue processing the weekly CSV with Python's built-in csv module and add no dependency.
advantages: Runs on any machine with Python installed and no install step, matching the single-script deployment on the analyst's laptop.
The current implementation streams rows with a generator, so memory use stays bounded regardless of file size.
No packages to pin, upgrade, or track for security advisories.
disadvantages: Any aggregation beyond simple iteration, such as grouping, joins, or column typing, must be hand-written.
A row count offers little headroom if the weekly report is expected to grow into richer summaries.
assumptions: The report's required output stays close to simple per-file summaries.
Weekly files are read once per run and fit on the analyst's disk.

alternatives.name: Add a Data-Handling Dependency (pandas or polars)
alternatives.description: Introduce a data-handling library such as pandas or polars and perform the CSV summarization through it.
advantages: Group-by, filtering, joins, and column typing are available immediately if the report grows.
Columnar engines can process large files faster than hand-written row loops.
disadvantages: Requires installing and managing packages on the analyst's laptop, where no environment is currently managed because no manifest exists.
Adds a large dependency surface, including transitive packages and upgrade and security tracking, to a small script.
pandas loads the whole frame into memory by default, which is untested against the unmeasured and highly variable weekly file sizes.
assumptions: The analyst can install and maintain Python packages on the laptop.
Future summaries will need operations that csv plus plain Python handles poorly.

alternatives.name: Keep stdlib csv Now and Measure File Sizes First
alternatives.description: Keep the standard-library implementation and record weekly file sizes and runtimes for a few cycles, then revisit the dependency question with data.
advantages: Resolves the documented unknown that nobody has measured how large the weekly files get.
Avoids installing a dependency until a concrete need is demonstrated.
disadvantages: Delays any richer reporting capability until the measurement period ends.
Requires a small process change to log sizes and timings and the discipline to collect data over several weeks.
assumptions: Weekly cycles continue long enough to collect representative samples.
The current row-count output remains sufficient during the measurement period.

criteria.name: Requirement fit
rubric: Blocks or complicates the current weekly summary report
Neutral for the current weekly summary report
Serves the current weekly summary report directly with no extra machinery

criteria.name: Maintenance burden
rubric: Adds a dependency surface to pin, upgrade, and monitor
No new dependency surface beyond the existing script

criteria.name: Capability headroom
rubric: No added capability if the report grows
Some added capability for near-term report growth
Broad ready-made capability for grouping, joins, and larger data

criteria.name: Setup portability
rubric: Requires a managed environment with installed packages on each machine
Runs with any stock Python installation

criteria.name: Robustness to unmeasured file sizes
rubric: Degrades or exhausts memory when weekly files turn out to be very large
Memory-safe for any file size, but real sizes remain unmeasured
Memory-safe for any file size and grounded in measured file-size data
